key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects, making PEA2PbI4 more resistant to ambient light and thermal degradation than BA2PbI4.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve two-dimensional perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural engineering, surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy to investigate degradation.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess chemical changes.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA2PbI4 degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative lifetime or solar-cell efficiency results, so improved material stability should not be equated with demonstrated device performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
